content.text: I thought this was an issue with the Java web app.  Is this is a problem with the flash widget?  If so, someone else to take this one.
Yes, this is an issue on the flex-based web admin (which runs in flash).
Narrowed this down a bit - In my browser (Firefox, Flash 10), I get an error that jsUploadComplete is not a function.
Apparently, Flash can dynamically export functions so that they are available to javascript.  This occurs in FedoraAdministrator.mxml in the fcrepo-client-webamin module, around line 256:
if (ExternalInterface.available) {
ExternalInterface.addCallback("jsUploadComplete",  jsUploadComplete);
ExternalInterface.call("upload",ingestUrl);

not exactly sure how debug/verify the interhal behaviour of Flash, but it seems that the problem could be here somewhere, and Flash it is not (or is not able to) export the necessary hooks for Javascript

Problem still exists in Flash 10.1.r53.  In Firefox the upload of managed content completes but the pop-up progress dialog is never closed.  In Explorer 7, the upload causes the browser to lock up and must be killed.

Just a note that the upload capability in the web admin actually jumps out of the Flash/Flex world and makes use of javascript to allow the selection and upload of files. The reason for this departure is because currently Flash cannot handle file uploads over https. See
http://bugs.adobe.com/jira/browse/FP-1044
and
https://bugs.adobe.com/jira/browse/FP-201
. If these issues are ever resolved, the file upload function of the web admin should be handled by Flex directly.
Moved to 3.5, not enough time to complete for 3.4
Reducing scope for 3.5 to displaying a message explaining current behaviour
This now appears to be working fine - can anyone else verify?
I can now verify that this is not fixed (3.5-SNAPSHOT)
No further releases planned for 3.x

When using the web admin to add a managed datastream from a local file (using Firefox) the dialog which allows you to select the file is never removed, even after the file upload to Fedora has completed. This makes it appear as if the file upload is hung, but the datastream is actually created properly, the dialog box is simply not removed.
Windows/Firefox
